findings.text: The browser and Servex now pick the same session, but they still use different time limits. The browser joins within 30 minutes (`JOIN_IDLE_MS`, ux/Dictate/chat.js:17), and `maybe_offer` shows "Pick up where you left off?" after 30 minutes. Servex's `create()` (Servex/agents/Sessions.js:881) resumes anything within `resume_ms` = 60 minutes (Sessions.js:244), and now does it project-wide. So for a session idle 30–60 minutes, the offer appears, the owner ignores it and speaks, and Servex joins that same session anyway. findings.md's "removes the 30-60 min gap" is not true. Use one limit on both sides.

The owner's main complaint ("a random message popped into the chat") can still happen. When `ensure()` silently joins a session idle under 30 minutes, the drawer attaches only after the first sentence, and `attach()` replays the whole file then. Old lines still appear under "can you hear me?" (ux/Dictate/chat.js:307-321). Show the joined session before the first sentence, or mark the replayed lines as earlier history. Also test it.

The new `draw()` guard (ux/Dictate/chat.js:243) is the fix for "a message from session A never shows in session B", but no test covers it. The brief says "test first". `active-session.mjs` tests 5 and 6 cover `latest_voice` and switching, not a late line stamped for the session just left.

Three docs still describe the old per-page resume. They need to say project-wide: ext/Session/readme.md:7 ("continues this page's from the last hour"), Servex/agents/doc/architecture.md:22 ("continue this page's session from the last hour"), and ext/Session/doc/architecture.md:14. ux/Dictate/doc/chat-notes.md:17 ("Resume offer timing": "the tab's newest OLDER session … within the hour") is stale too. The offer is now the project's newest voice session after 30 minutes.

`Sessions.create()` with no card now does what `Layers.session_for()` already does (Servex/agents/Layers.js:584-591): resume the project's newest session within `resume_ms`. That leaves two copies of one rule, and they already differ: Layers doesn't filter to `v-` sessions. Have one call the other.

The ask "a reply always goes to the session its question came from" has no test and no explicit answer in findings.md. The findings imply it already held: the smart seat answered in `v-qfzrnhh`, where the sentence was sent. Say so in one line.

Checked: `node Servex/agents/Sessions.test.mjs` in the worktree prints "29 checks passed". The change in Servex needs a Servex restart, and findings.md says so. A fresh agent could continue from findings.md plus this review.

The diff commits unrelated `files.jsonl` churn. The worst one is `ux/Dictate/playground/walkthrough/shots/files.jsonl` (+6 lines), which marks all six walkthrough pngs as `gone`. The worktree just lacks them, but they exist on michael/dev, so after the merge that index would be wrong. Drop the hunks in the 6 `files.jsonl` files from both commits, since the brief says "commit by path".

The silent join before the first sentence has no test. That is `maybe_offer` calling `resume_to` within `JOIN_IDLE_MS` (ux/Dictate/chat.js:305), the fix for the owner's "random message popped into the chat". The first review asked "Also test it". Tests 5 and 6 in `ux/Dictate/test/active-session.mjs` cover `latest_voice`, `is_other_session` and switching, but not "open the drawer with a session that spoke 5 minutes ago: its history is on screen and nothing new draws under the first sentence".

Test 5's guard check calls `is_other_session` directly. It does not prove that a late line from the session just left is dropped by `draw()` in a mounted chat. That is enough for a one-line guard, but an end-to-end check would match the brief's "test first" better.

The ask "a reply always goes to the session its question came from" still has no test and no sentence in findings.md (first review, note 6). Its evidence suggests this already held (the smart seat answered in `v-qfzrnhh` 4 s later). Say so in one line.

There are still two copies of the "resume the project's newest session" rule: `Sessions.create()` (Servex/agents/Sessions.js:880-884) and `Layers.session_for()` (Servex/agents/Layers.js:584). Only the first filters to `v-` sessions and uses `idle_ms` (first review, note 5). This is worth one shared method.

One comment is stale: Servex/agents/Sessions.js:882-883 still says "a session on this page spoke within `resume_ms`", but with no card it is now project-wide and `idle_ms`. Also, `idle_ms` doubles as the pair-sleep timer (Sessions.js:1495), so setting `SERVEX_SESSION_IDLE_MS` now moves the resume window too. A line in the comment would say so.

Checked: in the worktree, `node Servex/agents/Sessions.test.mjs` prints "29 checks passed". First review fixes 1, 3 and 4 are done: one 30-minute window on both sides, a guard test, and all four docs reworded. The Servex change needs a restart, which is vscode-mastermind's, and findings.md says so. A fresh agent could continue from findings.md plus the two reviews.
